elements.element: Customer may assign to an affiliate without consent.
elements.evidence: The approval exception expressly permits Client to assign to an affiliate without approval.

elements.element: Customer may assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets without consent.
elements.evidence: The approval exception expressly permits Client to assign to a successor in a merger, acquisition, or sale of substantially all assets.

elements.element: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent.
elements.evidence: TrueLink remains subject to the requirement for Client's prior written approval, because the exception applies only to Client.

elements.element: Customer's consent to Vendor assignment is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: The mutual prior-written-approval requirement is expressly qualified as “not to be unreasonably withheld.”

elements.element: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor.
elements.evidence: The clause states that TrueLink shall never assign or transfer its rights to a competitor of Client.

elements.element: Customer's change of control gives Vendor no termination right.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that a change of control of Client gives TrueLink no right to terminate the Agreement.

elements.element: Both parties may assign to a successor.
elements.evidence: Only Client receives a no-approval right to assign to a successor; TrueLink requires Client's prior written approval and may never assign to a Client competitor.

elements.element: A successor assignment requires written notice.
elements.evidence: No written-notice obligation applies to Client's successor assignments; the clause instead requires prior written approval for TrueLink assignments.
Client may also assign to an affiliate without approval, even though an affiliate assignment need not be a successor assignment.

elements.element: Consent to other assignments is not to be unreasonably withheld.
elements.evidence: Where prior written approval is required, it is expressly stated to be “not to be unreasonably withheld.”
